subject.title: Reduce tool schema token overhead (~3,500 tok/session)

question: Which default policy and implementation sequence should OpenClaw use to reduce model-facing tool-schema overhead without breaking cross-channel cron or isolated agents, provider schema contracts, plugin tools, or prompt-cache stability?
rationale: The remaining work changes default prompt/schema visibility across agent runtime, providers, channel compatibility, plugins, Tool Search, and possible config behavior, so maintainer intent is required before implementation.

options.title: Sequence Narrow Reductions
options.body: Keep this tracker open and land small measured PRs for duplicate Tooling text, empty-tool definitions, safe message-schema pruning, shorter descriptions, and deferred or slim schema design.

options.title: Defer To Focused Issues
options.body: Use narrower open issues for each remaining slice and close the umbrella only after maintainers decide the broad tracker no longer adds coordination value.

options.title: Adopt Aggressive Lazy Defaults
options.body: Make lazy or slim schemas the default now, accepting a broader compatibility and provider-contract review burden up front.

recommendation.title: Sequence Narrow Reductions
recommendation.body: Keep this tracker open and land small measured PRs for duplicate Tooling text, empty-tool definitions, safe message-schema pruning, shorter descriptions, and deferred or slim schema design.

likelyOwner.reason: The current source history and issue discussion make steipete the best available owner for prompt/runtime schema sequencing.
